INT-13's RLWM+LBA joint choice/RT and proactive-bound operators differ from INT-01's CRP task-set posterior/meta-policy operators; shared generic softmax/RL/WM vocabulary is not family identity.

Both use a CRP-related clustering constituent, but INT-01 clusters context-specific task-set/action-policy mappings whereas INT-14 clusters graph states into connected hierarchy H and uses posterior MCMC plus hierarchical planning. Whole historical family remains underdetermined.
INT-15 models MB/MF value conflict inside a drift-diffusion decision layer; INT-01 models task-set abstraction/reuse and meta-policy selection without the INT-15 trial-internal DDM operator.

INT-13's state is RL/WM action values plus response accumulators and set-size-dependent decision bounds; INT-14's state is a latent graph hierarchy inferred by MCMC and used by hierarchical shortest-path planning.

Both use reinforcement-learning-derived values in decision modeling, but INT-13 couples RLWM to LBA choice/RT dynamics with proactive set-size bounds, while INT-15 couples MB/MF values and conflict regressors to a DDM. No direct shared model ancestry is established.
